_doc: Division-level SOTP templates for conglomerate holding companies.
These three route to Financials/Holding Company, whose anchor `SOTP / NAV`
carries 0.70 weight and is implementable: False -- so 70% of a holdco's
valuation was a proxy. A bottom-up segment model is not the answer either:
their filings do not publish segment BALANCE SHEETS, so there is no basis
for a per-division equity bridge.
The practitioner method is a look-through: mark every listed stake at
MARKET (shares x price, never carrying value), value the unlisted operating
divisions on peer EV/EBITDA, sum, then apply a holding-company discount.
stake_pct = null means the ownership percentage is NOT yet sourced. Those
divisions are SKIPPED and the run is flagged incomplete rather than being
silently valued at zero or at a guessed stake -- a wrong ownership
percentage on a listed subsidiary moves the answer more than any multiple.

v2: ownership percentages sourced, and the two SGX holdcos added. PCRD holds 22.69% of PCCW plus a 1.92% DIRECT stake in HKT -- it does NOT hold a material direct stake in Singtel, which an earlier draft of this file wrongly recorded. Parts are converted to the holdco's reporting currency before being summed: Astra is quoted in IDR at ~190 trillion rupiah against a SGD parent, so an unconverted sum would be that one line and nothing else.

v3: five more templates from user-supplied ownership percentages with filing context (Kingboard/Laminates 61.74%, ThaiBev/F&N 69.61%, Wilmar/YKA 89.99% and AWL 56.94%, GenScript/Legend 45.03%). Each pairs its listed stakes with ONE stub division so the residual-EBITDA rule can complete them: group EBITDA less the whole of each CONSOLIDATED subsidiary's. Legend is an associate and is therefore not subtracted. Every stub multiple_range is an ASSUMPTION and says so in its source field -- the ownership percentages are sourced, the multiples are not.

v4: holdco discounts set by the user per name, replacing the placeholders. Two are STAKE-level, not group-level -- Kingboard 25% on the Laminates holding, GenScript 20% on the Legend mark -- so `discount_pct` now exists on a division and those two carry a group discount of zero. Discounts compose one way only: division first, group once on the total. Each template records the reasoning in `discount_source`.

v6: Olam and SingPost added with segment economics recorded in the template -- SGX publishes no machine-readable segment note, so the figures are user-supplied FY2024 / FY23-24 and each division states its own fiscal_year and source. Four bases beyond market_stake: transaction_anchor (a completed deal priced the division), cap_rate (income over a yield, for property), ev_ebit_range (stated EBIT against a peer band) and nil (an explicit, reasoned zero, which is not the same as a missing division). ThaiBev's template correctly excludes Frasers Property -- the ~28.78% stake was transferred to TCC Assets in the September 2024 swap that took F&N to 69.61%.

v6a: stated-figure divisions declare units_multiplier = 1e6. The published segment tables are in millions while market caps and net debt are absolute; without the scale the bridge subtracted a 13.8bn net debt from a 12,139 gross asset value and returned negative equity.

v6b: Olam's template currency is SGD, not USD. Divisions stay in their reported USD and convert per-division; the TEMPLATE currency has to be the listing currency because parent net debt reaches the bridge in it. Stated in USD, the bridge subtracted an SGD net debt from a USD gross asset value.

v10: Anta Sports (02020.HK) added -- the first CNY-reporting HK-listed template, and the first whose only listed stake is a US-listed ASSOCIATE below 50% (Amer Sports at 42.5% through AS Holding). Two consequences. The TEMPLATE currency is HKD while the statements are CNY, which is the v6b rule: parent net debt reaches the bridge in the listing currency, and residual_ebitda converts the CNY group EBITDA to HKD itself. And because Amer is under 50% it is equity-accounted, so residual_ebitda correctly subtracts nothing from group EBITDA and parent_net_debt correctly removes nothing from consolidated net debt -- the same shape as GenScript's Legend. The owner's 15% discount is applied at STAKE level with a group discount of zero, following v4. The core multiple band is SOURCED, not an assumption: nine peers measured on annual FY rows with every market cap cross-checked against price x shares. Anta's Puma stake is left unmarked because its percentage is not sourced. Also wired into _LOOKTHROUGH_PROMOTE so the template runs deterministically instead of waiting on an analyst PDF note.

v11: the 02020.HK net-debt note is CORRECTED, not the bridge. The note quoted CNY 20.590bn of net debt at the 2025 year end, which is FMP's raw `netDebt` field -- total debt less cash and equivalents only -- and the engine's `_net_debt_net_of_investments` counts short-term investments as cash, precisely to stop that figure being used. Anta holds CNY 26.206bn of them, so the same year end is CNY 5.616bn of net CASH and the 30-Jun-2026 interim the engine refreshes to is CNY 11.1bn of net cash, HKD 12.959bn. The bridge therefore ADDS liquidity where the note said it deducted debt, a HKD 37.125bn swing, and the published `SOTP / NAV` leg is HKD 93.68/share (+30.1% on a HKD 72.00 close) rather than the HKD 81.03 the note previewed. No shipped code used the bad figure -- `value_per_share` takes net debt from its caller and this template has no `net_debt_override` -- so this is a documentation fix, found by running the name in production. Two general lessons are recorded in the notes: quote the LATEST QUARTER the way S08.SI and C38U.SI do, and never state a net-debt figure without saying which liquidity definition it uses. The corrected note also records that the look-through leg is SCENARIO-INVARIANT, so promoting it to anchor puts a scenario-blind number at the largest weight in the blend, and WITHDRAWS the claim that the 7-11x band straddles the price: on net cash the band low reads +7.3% and the high +53.3%, so the whole band sits above the HKD 72.00 close and the +10%-to-price convention the promote is documented against does not hold anywhere in it.

02020.HK.name: Anta Sports Products
02020.HK.discount_source: 15% applied to the AMER SPORTS EQUITY MARK, not to the group, so holdco_discount is [0.0, 0.0]. Owner-set, matching the curated snapshot discount established for 09988.HK and other Chinese consumer-tech holding structures. A conglomerate operating direct retail (ANTA, FILA) alongside a listed associate faces moderate governance, double-tax and liquidity friction, but not the deep 25-30% of a multi-industry conglomerate or an unlisted holdco. Placed at STAKE level per this file's v4 rule that discounts compose one way only -- division first, group once on the total -- which is exactly how GenScript takes 20% on Legend and zero on the group. A group-level 15% would also have taken the haircut off the ANTA and FILA operating businesses, which the owner's stated rationale does not describe; the frictions named are all frictions of HOLDING THE ASSOCIATE.

divisions.name: Amer Sports
divisions.source: ~42.5% economic interest in Amer Sports Inc (NYSE: AS), held through AS Holding with FountainVest. Owner-supplied from post-IPO SEC filings and Anta's interim reports, 18 Sep 2026. Amer IPO'd on the NYSE in Feb 2024, so the stake is marked at MARKET (shares x price), never at carrying value: market cap USD 15.304bn measured 17 Sep 2026, cross-checked at USD 26.27 x 563.1m shares = USD 14.79bn, a 3.5% divergence. Converted at USD->HKD 7.84486 to HKD 51.025bn gross, HKD 43.371bn after the 15% stake haircut. Equity-accounted and below 50%, so residual_ebitda subtracts none of its EBITDA from the group figure and parent_net_debt removes none of its borrowings -- both correct, because neither was ever consolidated.

divisions.name: ANTA, FILA, Descente and Kolon Sport
divisions.source: Group EBITDA CNY 20.508bn on revenue CNY 80.219bn (FY2025, 31 Dec 2025, a 25.6% margin), which ALREADY EXCLUDES Amer Sports: a 42.5% associate under the equity method, so only Anta's share of Amer's net profit appears, below operating profit, and none of its revenue or EBITDA is consolidated. residual_ebitda measured returning HKD 24.070bn, exactly the CNY figure x 1.17371 with a ratio of 1.000 -- nothing subtracted, correct for a stake below 50%. 7-11x EV/EBITDA. Peer set measured on FMP annual FY rows at 17 Sep 2026, EV built as market_cap x fx(listing->reporting) + total_debt - cash, each market cap cross-checked against price x shares and agreeing within 5% on all six names tested: Top Sports 6110.HK 2.0x (11.2% margin), Li Ning 2331.HK 2.6x (16.7%), Xtep 1368.HK 3.4x (15.1%), Lululemon 4.1x (24.6%), ASICS 5.3x (15.4%), Bosideng 3998.HK 7.3x (22.7%), adidas 9.8x (12.5%), Nike 12.5x (9.9%), On Holding 20.5x (12.0%); set median 5.3x. The LOW end is Bosideng at 7.3x -- the closest margin comp to Anta's 25.6% among the domestic names, and effectively the multiple the market is ALREADY paying for Anta's core once the Amer stake is stripped out of group EV (measured 7.17x undiscounted, 7.49x with the 15% stake haircut; group EV HKD 223.657bn = HKD 199.490bn market cap + HKD 24.166bn net debt, less the stake's HKD 51.025bn gross / HKD 43.371bn net of the haircut). The HIGH end brackets adidas 9.8x and Nike 12.5x, a global-brand multiple for a business compounding double digits at a 25.6% margin. The set median of 5.3x is deliberately NOT used: it is dragged down by HK mass-market names on 11-17% margins, and margin is not what sets the multiple in this set (Lululemon 4.1x on 24.6% against On Holding 20.5x on 12.0%). PREVIEW, CORRECTED 2026-09-18. The first preview quoted HKD 81.21/share, +12.8%, 'inside the +10%-to-price convention recorded for BN4.SI and U96.SI', with band ends at -10.2% and +35.8% so that 'the band STRADDLES the price rather than asserting upside'. EVERY ONE OF THOSE NUMBERS WAS COMPUTED WITH HKD 24.166bn OF NET DEBT, which is FMP's raw `netDebt` field; the engine nets short-term investments and this name holds CNY 26.206bn of them, so the bridge is handed HKD 12.959bn of net CASH and ADDS it. See net_debt_note. WHAT PRODUCTION ACTUALLY PUBLISHES, run bda1622f on 2026-09-18 at a HKD 72.00 close: the `SOTP / NAV` leg is HKD 93.68/share, +30.1%. Reproduced offline to HKD 93.81 (0.14% away, market cap and FX drift between the probe and the run) as (24.011bn x 9.0 + 43.371bn + 12.959bn) / 2.904bn. THE STRADDLE CLAIM IS WITHDRAWN: on the corrected net cash the 7.0x band low reads HKD 77.27, +7.3%, and the 11.0x high HKD 110.35, +53.3%, so the ENTIRE band sits above the close and the +10% convention does not hold anywhere in it. Each turn of the multiple is worth HKD 8.27/share (24.011bn EBITDA / 2.904bn shares). At the 5.33x peer median the leg reads HKD 63.47, -11.9%; at Anta's own 9.29x group multiple, HKD 96.21, +33.6% -- a 51.6% swing in NAV per share across a set the market prices 1.98x to 20.48x. The band WIDTH still does not matter: `_mid = ebitda * (lo+hi) / 2`, so a 7-11x band and a 9-9x band give byte-identical NAV, and the width reaches only the value_low/value_high disclosure. THE LEG IS ALSO SCENARIO-INVARIANT -- identical 93.68 in bear, base and bull -- because a market_stake marked at market and an ev_ebitda_range at a fixed midpoint have no scenario input. THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THIS TEMPLATE, NOT OF THE BRIDGE: `look_through_value` does carry a `scenario_toggles` parameter feeding `_apply_toggles`, which can substitute an entire division via `toggle` + `toggle_override`, and BIDU uses it for its Kunlunxin IPO bull case (declared False by default). 02020.HK declares no toggle, and the engine's single call site in `dcf_agent.py` passes no scenario argument at all -- so BIDU's lever is unreachable from production as well, and the +US$79/ADS its docstring prices can only ever be exercised by a test or a manual call. Promoting it to anchor therefore puts a scenario-blind number at the largest weight in the blend, and the published spread compresses to 113.45 / 133.63 / 153.65, 1.35x bear-to-bull, against 1.68x for ICE, 1.79x for V and 1.55x for SCHW on the same engine on the same day. Base IV published HKD 133.63, +85.6%, final action BUY. `sotp_breakdown` is null in the payload, so NONE of the parts, gross asset value, net asset value or net debt behind that 93.68 is disclosed anywhere in the run; it had to be reconstructed by arithmetic from the top-level `net_debt` field.

02020.HK.net_debt_note: CORRECTED 2026-09-18 after a production run; the first version of this note stated the wrong figure with the wrong sign and is quoted below so the correction is auditable. WHAT THE BRIDGE ACTUALLY DEDUCTS: net debt at the 30-Jun-2026 interim is CNY 11.1bn of NET CASH (cash 17.2bn + short-term investments 26.8bn less debt 33.0bn), HKD 12.959bn converted at 1.1704 -- so `value_per_share` ADDS it to gross asset value rather than subtracting it. At the 31-Dec-2025 year end the same convention gives CNY 5.616bn of net cash (12.845 + 26.206 - 33.435). THE ENGINE'S CONVENTION COUNTS SHORT-TERM INVESTMENTS AS CASH: `_net_debt_net_of_investments` exists because FMP's own `netDebt` field is total debt less cash and equivalents ONLY, and its docstring names this exact trap on Alibaba with the sign flip. THE ORIGINAL NOTE QUOTED THE RAW FIELD INSTEAD: 'Group net debt CNY 20.590bn at 31 Dec 2025 (total debt CNY 33.435bn less cash and equivalents CNY 12.845bn), HKD 24.166bn converted. The engine deducts it in full.' 20.590 is precisely `total_debt - cash_and_equivalents`, measured, and precisely what the helper corrects. The omission is the CNY 26.206bn short-term investments line. THE BRIDGE WAS NEVER WRONG -- it takes net debt from the caller and this template carries no `net_debt_override`, so no shipped code used the bad figure; only the documentation did, and this file's rule is that its sourced numbers are checked. Measured effect on the published leg: HKD 93.68/share in production (run bda1622f, 2026-09-18) against the HKD 81.03 this template previewed, a HKD 37.125bn / HKD 12.78-per-share swing, taking the premium to the HKD 72.00 close from +12.5% to +30.1%. Also corrected: this file's convention is to quote the LATEST QUARTER (S08.SI and C38U.SI both say 30 Jun 2026) because `_refresh_balance_sheet_from_latest_quarter` overlays the annual row with it; the original note quoted the year end. The rest of the original reasoning stands and is unchanged: the core division is an ENTERPRISE value (`ev_ebitda_range` is not in EQUITY_BASES) so parent debt has to reach the bridge or the SOTP counts debt-financed assets as equity; Amer is 42.5%, below the 50% threshold, so `parent_net_debt` removes none of its borrowings -- measured returning the consolidated figure unchanged, correct for an equity-accounted associate; and the TEMPLATE CURRENCY IS HKD, NOT CNY, although Anta REPORTS in CNY, per the v6b rule, since parent net debt reaches the bridge in the listing currency and `residual_ebitda` converts the CNY group EBITDA to HKD itself.
02020.HK.shares_note: The engine divides by 2.904bn line-item shares, not by the 2.771bn implied by market cap / price (HKD 199.490bn / HKD 72.00). The quote cross-check that exists to catch exactly this divergence is explicitly SKIPPED for HK and SG tickers, and 4.8% would not have cleared its 25% trigger anyway. Every per-share figure for this name -- the look-through NAV, the DCF, the multiples -- is therefore ~4.6% lower than it would be on the quote-implied count. Not corrected here; it is a pre-existing engine behaviour across every HK name, not a property of this template. The ratio is what is sourced, not the level: the per-share figures this note used to quote (HKD 81.21 on 2.904bn against HKD 85.12 on 2.771bn) were computed on the superseded net-debt figure and are corrected in net_debt_note; production publishes HKD 93.68 on the 2.904bn count.
